# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
Participants assigned to the control arm may cross over to the investigational therapy after progression; safety and efficacy analyses will follow the standard primary-analysis methods without any separate handling of post-crossover data.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
The pediatric expansion cohort will proceed under the adult development plan, with pediatric assessments documented separately and added to the pediatric study plan after the cohort is completed.
Dose selection for expansion will be based solely on the prespecified primary endpoint from the escalation cohort; no exploratory analyses of existing or newly accrued clinical databases will be conducted.
The recommended Phase 2 dose will be selected solely from dose-limiting toxicity rates observed during Cycle 1, without evaluating exposure, pharmacokinetic population parameters, or dose–response relationships.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.
In the pediatric expansion cohort, adverse events and protocol-specified toxicities will be assessed at scheduled visits, and liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated.
The medical monitor may be any licensed physician with general inpatient-care experience; prior oncology practice or clinical-trial oversight is not required.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(BOIN)이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_012.document_title: 항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인 (민원인 안내서)
ev_012.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

특정 상황에서의 조치 방법(예: 용량 조정)을 명확하게 기재해야 한다. 이와 같은

collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and

항암제 임상시험 중 용량 최적화 전략 가이드라인
 1. 서론
 항암제 초기 임상시험의 주된 목적 중 하나는 다음 단계의 임상시험에서 추가 평가가 
필요한 용량을 결정하는 것이다. 항암제는 약물의 작용기전과 투여받는 환자 집단의 
특수성으로 인해 암 치료 효과를 극대화하면서 부작용은 최소화 할 수 있는 적절한 
수준의 용량이 요구된다. 과도한 용량은 심각한 부작용을 유발할 수 있으며, 반대로 
부족한 용량은 암세포의 효과적인 제거가 어려워 결국 치료의 실패로 이어질 수 있다.
 본 가이드라인은 항암제 중 저분자(small molecule) 의약품의 임상시험에서 최적의 
용량을 파악하기 위한 전략을 구체적으로 안내함으로써 개발 및 제품화에 도움을 
주고자 마련하였다. 방사성 의약품, 세포 및 유전자 치료제, 암 치료 목적의 백신 및 
생약 성분의 항암제 등은 별도의 논의가 필요하며, 인체 최초 임상시험(First-in-human,
FIH)에서 시작 용량의 선택에 대한 내용은 포함하지 않는다.
2. 배경
 일반적으로 항암제의 권장 2상 용량(Recommended phase 2 dose, RP2D)을 결정하기 
위한 용량 탐색 시험은 용량 증량 및 용량 확장을 포함하며 최대 내약 용량(Maximal
tolerated dose, MTD)을 결정할 수 있도록 설계한다. 이는 세포독성 화학요법의 
용량-반응 곡선이 가파르고 약물 표적에 대한 특이성이 제한적이나, 심각하고 생명을 
위협하는 암 질환에 대한 효과적인 대안이 부족함으로 인해 상당한 독성은 감수할 
필요가 있음을 고려한 방법이다. MTD는 소수의 시험대상자에서 용량을 단계적으로 
증량하면서 짧은 기간 동안 중증 또는 생명을 위협하는 용량 제한 독성(Dose limiting
toxicity, DLT)이 사전에 지정된 비율까지 도달하는지 여부를 평가하여 결정한다. 또한 
일반적으로 후속 임상시험에서는 MTD 또는 MTD에 가까운 용량을 선정한다.
 키나제 억제제와 같이 최근 개발하는 항암제는 대부분 종양에 중요한 분자적 경로와 
상호 작용하도록 설계한다(즉 표적 치료제). 이와 같은 약물은 세포독성 화학요법 대비 
더 넓은 치료 지수를 가지면서 다른 용량-반응 관계를 나타내는 경우가 많기 때문에

Purpose of Dose-Response Information 
Knowledge of the relationships among dose, drug-concentration in blood, and clinical 
response (effectiveness and undesirable effects) is important for the safe and effective 
use of drugs in individual patients.  This information can help identify an appropriate 
starting dose, the best way to adjust dosage  to the needs of a particular patient, and a 
dose beyond which increases would be un likely to provide added benefit or would 
produce unacceptable side effects.  Dose-c oncentration, concentration- and/or dose-
response information is used to prepare dosage and administration instructions in 
product labeling.  In addition, knowledge of dose-response may provide an economical 
approach to global drug development, by enabling multiple regulatory agencies to 
make approval decisions from a common database. 
Historically, drugs have often been initially marketed at what were later recognized 
as excessive doses (i.e., doses well onto the plateau of the dose-response curve for the 
desired effect), sometimes with adverse co nsequences (e.g. hypokalemia and other 
metabolic disturbances with thiazide-type di uretics in hypertension).  This sit

Problems with Titration Designs 
A study design widely used to demonstrate  effectiveness utilizes dose titration to 
some effectiveness or safety endpoint.  Such titration designs, without careful 
analysis, are usually not informative about dose-response relationships.  In many 
studies there is a tendency to spontaneous improvement over time that is not easily 
distinguishable from an increased response to higher doses or cumulative drug 
exposure.  This leads to a tendency to choose, as a recommended dose, the highest

T00_protocol_scan.position: The synopsis states mutually inconsistent RP2D rules: integrated randomized assessment versus selection solely by Cycle 1 DLTs, excluding exposure and dose–response evidence. It also defers pediatric planning despite adult-only eligibility, describes an undefined control arm, and permits nonspecialist monitoring. Reconcile these provisions and provide supporting plans before the dose rationale can be assessed.

T01_structure_class.position: The stated covalent classification and SMILES alone do not establish a mismatch with external potency records or predict organ-specific toxicity. The supplied ChEMBL values distinguish cellular from biochemical assays but do not establish compound identity or comparability.

T02_target_evidence.position: The Open Targets record reports no safety liabilities, but that is not evidence of absence. The candidate-selection statement does not show how clinically relevant sotorasib-label safety findings or tolerability across doses enter selection.

T03_class_label_check.position: The stated liver-test schedule matches the frequency quoted from the sotorasib label; less frequent monitoring is not demonstrated. Appendix B is unavailable, and the truncated label excerpt cannot establish whether hepatotoxicity or pneumonitis modification rules align with the label.

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: Intensive escalation sampling supplies material for dose–exposure analysis, but randomized-cohort troughs alone do not describe full exposure at both candidates. This matters particularly given the label’s reported nonlinear, time-dependent PK; the stated RP2D rule also excludes exposure analyses.

T05_design_oc.position: The synopsis says four BOIN scenarios were simulated but provides no results. Whether the 36-subject maximum achieves acceptable selection or safety performance cannot be judged from the supplied material.

T06_regulatory_clause_search_KR.position: The pediatric cohort is proposed under an adult plan with pediatric assessments deferred, while synopsis eligibility starts at age 18. The MFDS dose-optimization document is a nonbinding civil guide, not a legal mandate. Cohort feasibility and justification remain unsupported.

T07_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: Randomizing at least 60 participants supports comparison in principle, but the synopsis does not justify whether enrollment adequately assesses safety and antitumor activity per dose, or specify cohort-specific objectives and stopping rules. FDA guidance offers nonbinding recommendations.

T08_analog_trial.position: A four-week immunotherapy washout is stated, but the supplied label excerpt does not establish a sufficient washout interval or quantify delayed hepatotoxicity risk. The protocol does not show a specific monitoring or risk-management rationale for recently exposed participants.
